stories.headline: Liberty's star trio say coach's future 'not our decision'
stories.summary: The Liberty's Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones fell short of offering a definitive vote of confidence in coach Chris DeMarco after they were swept by the Dream.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- After the Liberty were swept in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs, losing 85-83 to the Dream on Friday, first-year coach Chris DeMarco said without hesitation that he expects to return next season.

But when New York's three stars -- Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones -- were asked whether it was their hope and expectation that DeMarco would be back, none offered a definitive vote of confidence.

Stewart said she "1,000%" believes the team had the personnel to win a championship this year but added, "What I'm thinking about right now is just the missed opportunity."

"Of course, we want to win a championship every single time we step on the court, but it's really hard in this league, and in order to do that, you need to be consistent for the full 44 games," Stewart said when asked about DeMarco. "And I don't think we were consistent throughout the season. I think that we started to show some life and peak a little bit in towards the end and in the playoffs. But this is not like cramming for a test. You got to be ready and ready to go since the jump."

Ionescu said DeMarco's future was "not our decision," a sentiment that Stewart and Jones echoed.

"We're thankful for everything that he's done this year," Ionescu said. "Just focusing on the now, the way he's poured into us and stayed positive, level-headed through the ups and downs of this season as well that didn't go the way that he wanted either.

"I mean, I don't know what's going to happen. Regardless, thankful for him coaching us this year and obviously giving us a chance. And we just fell short."

Added Jones: "That's not our say. Our job is to go out there and play good basketball and represent the organization well, represent the fan base well, and our families. And I think we do a good job of focusing on that. And it is what it is."

After consecutive Finals appearances in this "superteam" iteration of the Liberty -- starting in 2023 when Stewart and Jones arrived -- New York fell short of that mark for the second consecutive year.

Stewart, Jones and Ionescu are all under contract for two more years, which likely represents, at minimum, the Liberty's current championship window.

"We went to the Finals two years in a row and haven't gone since. But it's really hard to get to the Finals," said Stewart, a three-time WNBA champion. "This s--- isn't easy, and when you get there and when you win, you can't take it for granted. ... You don't know if you'll be able to get back, and I feel like for us, we're not taking that for granted."

Added Ionescu: "It's not just go [to the Finals] -- it's win."

After more than a decade as an assistant with the Golden State Warriors, DeMarco was hired in December to replace Sandy Brondello, who was let go after four seasons at the helm and one year removed from leading the franchise to its first championship.

New York had an up-and-down 2026 season, starting 13-12 and ultimately earning the No. 8 seed in the playoffs. Player availability worked against them at times, as Ionescu and guard Leonie Fiebich missed significant time and Satou Sabally was limited to just 13 games before being ruled out for the season. Betnijah Laney-Hamilton fell out of the rotation and was waived four days after the trade deadline.

Players credited each other for sticking together through so many difficulties, and even Friday, DeMarco lauded his players for fighting "like hell" against Atlanta. But though the Liberty swept the No. 1 seed Minnesota Lynx in the first round, they looked far from a contender in the semifinals.

The Liberty's seasonlong flaws were exposed by the defensive-minded, athletic and ultra-connected Dream, who comfortably took care of New York despite playing without top scorer Allisha Gray for all but 11 minutes in the series.

"It just took a while to find our identity, what we were going to do defensively and how we were going to play with teams," Stewart said. "When people say defense wins championships, it's f---ing true."

Added Fiebich: "We won in '24 because we brought the toughness and we had the talent and we had the team chemistry. I think we've got to continue to find ways to get that back."

DeMarco's inexperience was on display as the postseason progressed, especially during the controversial end to Game 2, when he failed to use the Liberty's final reset timeout at the end of overtime or attempt to stop the game to clarify whether they had one.

DeMarco said he intends to take some time to assess the season.

"Not just myself -- staff, players, everything," he said. "The great part about what I do is that you're constantly learning, and there's new things you learn every single day, every season."

"I think they're great people," Fiebich said of the staff. "I think it was their first time in the WNBA. Maybe you could feel it here and there in some situations, but I think the most important thing was that we were out there as a group. It was a collaborative thing, and that was most important."

Stewart's play was a silver lining to the Liberty's frustrating 2026. The 32-year-old enjoyed a healthy year, playing 42 of 44 regular-season games and reminding the basketball world why she is considered one of the game's all-time greatest players. But that might make Friday's result feel even worse.

"Especially after being injured last season, I don't take for granted a healthy season, and that's what really pisses me off," Stewart said. "I couldn't really fulfill my full opportunity to make something spicy happen."

As the Liberty departed in disbelief and the Dream celebrated on the Barclays floor, Stewart -- experiencing her first WNBA playoffs sweep -- walked into the tunnel with a towel around her head in a rare display of emotion, which she said came from thinking about the fans.

Liberty fans waited 28 years for the team to win its first championship. They will now have to wait another year for the team to try to win its second.

"I know how much [the fans] have our back, and they really ride for us," Stewart said. "I wanted for us to continue to have a shot and extend this season and play for our fans. ... They deserve more too."

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix: George Russell crashes out of sprint after taking early lead
stories.summary: George Russell crashed out of the lead of the sprint race at the Singapore Grand Prix as his slim championship chances took another brutal blow.
stories.body:
SINGAPORE -- George Russell crashed out of the lead of the sprint race at the Singapore Grand Prix as his slim championship chances took another brutal blow.

Russell had beaten Max Verstappen down to Turn 1 in Saturday's sprint, which was delayed due to a pre-race shower and started with all drivers on the intermediate wet tyre.

As he rounded the final corner to start the second lap, Russell got wide on the kerb and slammed into the wall.

Russell's car went backwards across the race track and fortunately was not collected by any of the following drivers. "S---," Russell immediately said on the Mercedes team radio. "Sorry."

When asked if he was OK, he replied; "Ahhh. I'm fine. Sorry. Sorry. Sorry."

The crash immediately brought out a Safety Car.

The incident saw the British driver squander an opportunity to take some points out of teammate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who was in seventh when Russell crashed.

Antonelli benefitted from some late drama to gain more points, with McLaren teammates Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri colliding ahead of him on the final lap.

- When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races

- Max Verstappen claims sprint victory at Singapore Grand Prix, George Russell crashes out of lead

- 'Watch Teletubbies, not F1': Toto Wolff hits back at 'brainless' Kimi Antonelli driver favouritism claims

Antonelli finished fourth and gained five points to extend his lead over Russell to 89 points.

"Miscalculation," Russell told Sky Sports. "Came through the corner had more battery deployment than I thought, pushed me a little bit wider than I hoped and went onto the white line. Silly mistake. Big consequences."

Russell is set to start Sunday's race from the back of the grid due to a penalty for changing his engine after it failed at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend and looks set to go to Austin's U.S. Grand prix even further back.

Verstappen controlled the race after Russell's crash to claim his first sprint victory this season, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton second and Charles Leclerc third.

stories.headline: Can the Seahawks' defense again silence the 49ers' hot offense Sunday?
stories.summary: Seattle's defense stole the show the past two times these teams met. But the 49ers and Brock Purdy are on a roll heading into Week 5.
stories.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- It took Mike Macdonald several weeks to rewatch the Seattle Seahawks' 29-13 victory in Super Bowl LX. It was partly because of his packed schedule and partly because of his perfectionist ways. The head coach and defensive playcaller knew that even though his unit had dominated the New England Patriots, it had also made miscues that would eat at him once he saw them on film.

Macdonald had no such hang-ups about either of Seattle's two January victories over the San Francisco 49ers, a pair of defensive masterpieces in which the Seahawks held their divisional rivals out of the end zone -- first in Week 18, then again in the divisional round of the playoffs.

That was then.

The 49ers (4-0) and their offense are rolling heading into an NFC West clash with the Seahawks (3-1) on Sunday at Lumen Field. San Francisco ranks second in points per game (30.5), Brock Purdy leads the league in Total QBR (89.2), and the quarterback has a few playmakers who weren't on the team nine months ago.

"None of what happened last year matters," Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV said. "It's a new year, new season. They've got a hell of a group. They've put together four good games, won every one of them. Just like we have a new team, they've got a new team. They're doing some different things. We've just got to go out there and do our job."

In the first of two defensive performances that even Macdonald might have considered perfect, the Seahawks held Kyle Shanahan's team to 173 total yards in last year's regular-season finale, a winner-take-all affair in which the NFC West and No. 1 seed were on the line. Seattle intercepted one of Purdy's passes, forced two more turnovers on downs and limited Christian McCaffrey to 23 yards on eight carries in a 13-3 victory at Levi's Stadium.

When the Seahawks hosted the 49ers after their first-round bye, it was more of the same. Macdonald's top-ranked scoring defense allowed only 236 yards, generated three takeaways to go along with three more turnovers on downs, and bottled up McCaffrey again (35 rushing yards on 11 attempts) in a 41-6 rout.

While appearing on NBC's pregame coverage of Super Bowl LX, Shanahan said self-deprecatingly that his "expert opinion" on the Seahawks might not be worth much given that his offense couldn't generate a touchdown against them during the past two times they met.

"We tackled really well. We limited extra yardage. I thought we rushed the quarterback with discipline and married the coverage," Macdonald recalled this week. "That's what it takes to play really good football, in general. But the guys played hard, played physical, played well situationally."

Said safety Julian Love: "I think we communicated really well. I think these guys do a lot of stuff pre-snap, motions, shifts, crazy alignment-type things. For the most part, we have a good feel of our communication versus them. And then just man for man, understanding who you're lined up against. I think we match up well with them just body for body. I think that's our biggest advantage compared to any other team."

But the matchup is a bit different this time.

Cornerback Riq Woolen and safety Coby Bryant, who missed the Week 18 game, are two starters gone from the Seahawks' defense. That unit, which is allowing the fifth-fewest points (18.3) this season, will have defensive tackle Leonard Williams on Sunday despite an ankle injury that sidelined him for the end of their win last week over the Los Angeles Chargers.

The 49ers, meanwhile, brought back Deebo Samuel Sr. this summer after adding another veteran receiver in Mike Evans. They also didn't have tight end George Kittle in the divisional round game last season after he tore his Achilles a week earlier.

That trio has accounted for nine of Purdy's 11 touchdown passes, a figure that is tied for the league lead. He's completing nearly 70% of his passes, has thrown only one interception and has yet to be sacked.

"He's playing really good," Jones said, "getting the ball out really decisive, making the throws, not putting the ball in jeopardy. ... He's playing really smart, and then he's out there extending plays with his legs. He's doing it all right now, playing at a high level. We've got to go execute. We have to play at a high level because they are."

The 49ers won't have fullback Kyle Juszczyk. Though that is a significant loss given how much their offense relies on two-back sets -- they've led the NFL by a wide margin in percentage of snaps out of 21 personnel (two running backs, one tight end) under Shanahan -- it also creates a question for Macdonald of how San Francisco will adjust. Juszczyk has missed just seven games since entering the NFL in 2013.

"Kyle's been extremely durable over the years, so there's not a lot of things you can go to and see how they actually did it with the people that are on their current roster," Macdonald said. "Shoutout to him for being able to play all those games. I don't think they're going to end up in 11 personnel [one running back, one tight end] all game. I don't think that's how they want to operate. We'll have a plan for 11, but we're anticipating multiple tight end people out there, and we'll have to adjust throughout the game to test how we think they're going to play it."

There might be one more subplot to this game.

As if those two January losses didn't leave a bad enough taste in the 49ers' mouths, they might be extra motivated after having watched the Seahawks win the Super Bowl at Levi's Stadium, then celebrate in their locker room?

"They might feel a certain way," Love said. "I think regardless of what happened last year, we don't like them, they don't like us, straight up. They might not like us a little bit more because of what happened at the end of last season, but it is what it is. You know, it's going to be a fistfight against a division opponent. That's all of them. We don't like anybody in our division."

stories.headline: MLB division series: ALDS Game 5 live updates, takeaways, analysis
stories.summary: Who will move on to face the Rays? We've got it all covered.
stories.body:
It all comes down to this for the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox!

With two consecutive road wins in Chicago, the Guardians sent the American League Division Series back to Cleveland for a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday night. The winner gets an AL Championship Series date against the Tampa Bay Rays.

What will decide ALDS Game 5 and how will all the action play out? We've got you covered with pregame keys for both teams, lineups, live updates and takeaways from Cleveland.

Key links: Mega-preview | Series outlooks | Bracket | Schedule

First pitch: 8 p.m. ET

Game 5 starters: Sean Burke vs. Gavin Williams

What the White Sox must do to win: There is no mystery here. The White Sox need some length from Sean Burke. He gave it to them in their Game 2 win, throwing 5⅓ innings while giving up just one run. It's unclear if the bullpen's Game 4 implosion occurred because arms are tiring but why take the chance? Pound-for-pound, Burke has been the team's best starter all season -- if you can't rely on him now then Chicago doesn't deserve to advance. The way the playoffs are going, another 5⅓ will feel like a complete game -- and give the White Sox a great chance to win. -- Jesse Rogers

What the Guardians need to do to win: Gavin Williams & Co. have to keep the White Sox in the yard, as they've done well so far in the series. Chicago has been antsy at the plate in the series, expanding the zone and swinging big too often with runners on base. But it's also a team that ranked third in the AL with 211 homers. Long balls have often been contagious for the ChiSox, and Cleveland isn't likely to out-homer them in a slugfest.

At the plate, the hitters have to work counts like they did so well in Chicago. The White Sox's bullpen looked gassed in Games 3 and 4 but if Sean Burke gets on a roll, which he has done a number of times this season, he can get into the middle innings and shorten the workload of Chicago's relievers at the end of the game. Cleveland needs to get Will Venable's pitching merry-go-round spinning as early as possible in Game 5. -- Bradford Doolittle

Game 5 X factor: After closing out Game 4, Williams said he's ready to start in Game 5. "Seven, eight, nine innings," he told ESPN. "Whatever they need, I'm ready." Williams punched out 11 in Game 2, but the White Sox chased him after 98 pitches in five innings. So while, seven, eight, nine might be a stretch, the notion of efficiency is paramount to keep Guardians manager Stephen Vogt from needing to rely too heavily on a bullpen taxed by a trying series. Williams skipped his standard bullpen session Wednesday so he could throw in Game 4 Thursday. The Guardians can only hope he is indeed ready. -- Jeff Passan

Stat you need to know: The Guardians are the sixth team in playoff history to force a Game 5 after losing the first two games at home. Three of the other five teams won their series: 2015 Blue Jays (over the Rangers), 2012 Giants (over the Reds), 2001 Yankees (over the A's). The 2010 Rays and 1981 Brewers lost Game 5. But the key stat? Maybe it's the 50 pitches Cade Smith threw over Games 3 and 4. He tried to go two innings for the second game in a row in Game 4 but couldn't get an out in the ninth. After pitching in each of the first four games, will he have another two-inning stint in him? -- David Schoenfield

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previews, stats, betting info for Saturday's 14 games
stories.summary: It's a typically massive slate, from 1 p.m. ET all the way through two 10 p.m. starts. Get prepared here.
stories.body:
On Tuesday, hockey fans will enjoy the Frozen Frenzy with all 32 teams in action throughout the night. On Saturday, the NHL nearly gets there, with 14 games taking place.

The fun begins with Flyers-Bruins at 1 p.m. ET, continues with three more in the late afternoon, the standard phalanx of eight games at 7 or 7:30, then two nightcaps beginning at 10.

Here's a look at the key stats and storylines in each contest, along with betting info on broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Philadelphia Flyers at Boston Bruins

1 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | BOS -135, O/U: 5.5

One of these days, the Flyers will get their first win of the season. Will it be Saturday? The Bruins have alternated between being world-beaters -- including impressive wins over the Mammoth and Rangers -- and getting their doors blown off by the Senators and Wild. This game could go a lot of different directions!

Vancouver Canucks at New Jersey Devils

3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -278, O/U: 6.5

In seasons past, any Canucks-Devils game would mean a showdown between Vancouver's Quinn Hughes and New Jersey's Jack Hughes (and later, Luke Hughes). With Quinn now in Minnesota, the familial connection isn't there. But this could be a fun watch, since Canucks center Elias Pettersson has apparently remembered that he's an elite talent; after two straight lackluster campaigns, he has eight points through the first five games. How will the Devs' own superstars match up?

Edmonton Oilers at San Jose Sharks

4 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | EDM -155, O/U: 6.5

Is the main event taking place at 4 p.m. Saturday? This is the first showdown of the season between the world's No. 1 player, Connor McDavid, and Macklin Celebrini, who might be his toughest competition in the MVP race for years to come. Don't miss this one; the teams don't play again until Jan. 13.

Minnesota Wild at Florida Panthers

6 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -135, O/U: 6.5

For those who dug the 2026 Olympics -- and Team USA's gold medal win -- there are a number of familiar faces here. Minnesota will have Quinn Hughes and Matt Boldy in the lineup (Brock Faber is out injured following surgery for a skull fracture), and Florida's forward group includes Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk.

Utah Mammoth at Buffalo Sabres

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -108, O/U: 6.5

On Friday, Greg Wyshynski identified 40 players who are breakout candidates; that list included current Bruin JJ Peterka, who previously skated for both the Mammoth and Sabres. In addition to the Peterka connection, both of these teams can consider themselves legit Stanley Cup contenders this season, and this is a rare showdown between the interconference foes.

Detroit Red Wings at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -218, O/U: 6.5

There's something special about an Original Six matchup, particularly one featuring arguably the two greatest uniforms in professional sports history. Both teams are still figuring things out a bit, but perhaps one of the two gets on track here.

Nashville Predators at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -162, O/U: 5.5

One reason the Canadiens don't have the record some expected is because the Predators beat them 5-2 the other night, though that score is a little misleading given that Adam Edstrom scored two empty-netters in the final three minutes. Can the Senators avoid a similar fate? Through three games, goaltender Linus Ullmark looks like the dominant version of himself that kept things interesting in the 2026 playoffs, with a .956 save percentage and three W's.

Dallas Stars at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -155, O/U: 6.5

For those with quite long memories, you'll remember these two franchises squared off in the 1991 Stanley Cup Final (with the Stars then known as the Minnesota North Stars). The good news for Dallas is that Mario Lemieux, Paul Coffey and Jaromir Jagr won't be playing Saturday. The bad news is that Sidney Crosby, Erik Karlsson and Evgeni Malkin will. Can Jake Oettinger (.967 save percentage in three games) hold the Penguins down enough for the Stars to outscore them?

Carolina Hurricanes at Chicago Blackhawks

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -230, O/U: 5.5

As the defending Cup champs, the Hurricanes will typically "get every team's best," as coach Rod Brind'Amour said earlier this season. DraftKings does not believe that will put them in too much peril against the Blackhawks, but stranger things have happened!

Columbus Blue Jackets at St. Louis Blues

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | STL -125, O/U: 5.5

For some reason, the Blue Jackets have played only two games so far, which means they should be plenty fresh for this showdown against Robert Thomas & Co. And for those who like goaltending, two of the best young ones in the league may be squaring off in Joel Hofer (St. Louis) and Jet Greaves (Columbus).

Toronto Maple Leafs at Colorado Avalanche

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | COL -205, O/U: 6.5

This is the middle game of a three-game set for the Leafs against the top Western Conference contenders. They earned a point with a shootout loss against the Golden Knights on Thursday. Will this one be as close? On the other side, the Avalanche offense is en fuego to begin the campaign. According to ESPN Research, Colorado's 23 goals through four games are the most by an NHL team since the 1993-94 Kings.

Tampa Bay Lightning at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -170, O/U: 5.5

Two things that caught many a reader's eye about the Top 100 player rankings this week: the Lightning tied for the most players on the list (six), despite not getting past the first round of the playoffs since 2022, and Islanders second-year pro Matthew Schaefer being ranked No. 16. Maybe the result of this game will let us know which of those two things is more outlandish.

Anaheim Ducks at Calgary Flames

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | ANA -125, O/U: 6.5

Like the Flyers, the Flames are also searching for win No. 1 this season; of course, expectations for Calgary were not quite as high as those for Philly. Anaheim will be playing this one as the second leg of a back-to-back after playing the Jets in Winnipeg on Friday.

Los Angeles Kings at Vegas Golden Knights

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -162, O/U: 5.5

When the Golden Knights entered the NHL in the 2017-18 season, many thought there would be a natural rivalry with the Kings. It has resulted in just one playoff series thus far -- a sweep by Vegas in 2018 -- and a 21-15-4 edge for the Golden Knights in 40 regular-season contests. With the Kings now embarking on the post-Anze Kopitar era, it's not entirely surprising that they've struggled out of the starting blocks, while the Knights are atop the Pacific Division at 4-1-0 and Jack Eichel is among the league scoring leaders. But that's why they play the games; perhaps this one reverses the trend for both clubs.

Reminder: Fans can catch all the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Miami coach urges MLS fans to enjoy Lionel Messi after Argentina adiós
stories.summary: Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González said Argentina will miss Lionel Messi following the captain's international retirement before urging fans to enjoy his time with the MLS club.
stories.body:
Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said Argentina will miss Lionel Messi terribly following the captain's international retirement before urging fans to enjoy his time with the MLS club.

"[The farewell match] was incredibly intense," González said on Friday. "Obviously, I was very close to him, but ultimately, that moment belonged to him, it was his time.

"All that mattered was for him to enjoy it. I just told him to enjoy it, to soak up all the love, not just from Argentina, but from the whole world.

"He'll be missed in that jersey, of course, but today we have him here, and we have to enjoy having him with us now.

"He's going to miss it, from the day he retires until the day he's no longer around. I have no doubt that, for him, the national team was all about wearing that jersey; he'll always miss the mark he left and the legacy he created there. But unfortunately, we won't see him in that jersey anymore, so those of us here have to enjoy it. Now he's ours, so I have to enjoy it."

González added that Messi left a lasting legacy with Argentina due to his competitive nature, inspiring those around him to improve every day.

"Leo is someone who conveys a certain mindset every day; he demands that his teammates, and all of us, give 100% in every respect," González said.

"He's a born competitor. You see it in every training session, and it's incredible. He's 39 years old, yet he's constantly seeking out new challenges. That's fantastic for everyone, not just his teammates, but the staff and the club as well.

"He pushes you to be better every single day.

"That's why he's such an example; as I said before, he'll be missed on the national team because he left a legacy there, and he's leaving a legacy here too, the club changed the day he arrived.

"He drives us to improve daily and to be prepared in every way. And he's happy, I see him enjoying himself, and that makes me very happy, too."

Messi and Inter Miami now prepare to face D.C. United on Saturday night at Nu Stadium in the first game back after the international break.

"We're in a good place. The guys who returned from their respective national teams are doing really well," González said. "We've trained effectively, and we know we need to get back to winning, that's a given. We have a few matches to settle in properly, reach the final stretch of the season in top form, and fine-tune the details so we can be the best team possible."

Inter Miami currently sits in third place on the Eastern Conference table with 46 points in 27 games following a five-match winless streak in MLS. The Herons recorded one loss and four draws in their last five regular-season MLS games.

Inter Miami did, however, defeat Cruz Azul 2-0 in the Campeones Cup on Sept. 16.

"We have a very clear idea of what we want and what we're aiming for. Defensively, we need to be much better; we're facing an opponent that relies heavily on transitions and is very dangerous in those situations, so we have to guard against that.

"At the same time, we can't lose sight of the fact that we need to take the initiative and go out to win the match. As I just said, we need to get back to winning ways, and hopefully, we can achieve that."

Inter Miami will then host New York City FC on Oct. 14 at Nu Stadium.

stories.headline: Jake Paul cleared to fight; Canelo, Strickland, others on wish list
stories.summary: Jake Paul, who has been cleared to resume fighting after recovering from a broken jaw, has a list of big names he'd like to face in boxing and MMA now that he's back.
stories.body:
Jake Paul has been medically cleared to return to boxing.

Paul (12-2, seven KOs), 29, has not fought since he suffered a broken jaw during his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua last December. Paul underwent surgical procedures on his jaw in December and February. Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder of Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, officially updated Paul's status Thursday.

"Jake Paul has been cleared to return to the boxing ring," Bidarian wrote on X.

Paul told ESPN in April that he'd resumed light training but had not been cleared to spar. He has targeted a full return to competition in early 2027.

In connection to the update on his health, Paul provided his latest wish list of eventual fights this week. The list included 15 potential fights, including Canelo Alvarez, Ryan Garcia, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder in boxing as well as mixed martial arts contests against Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz.

The list also included UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland (31-7), who linked himself to Paul this week in a series of online posts expressing frustration about his UFC contract.

"I gotta be honest, unless things change with the UFC I'm kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 seconds and they don't want to pay us a fraction of it. Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds], knocking out my contract and scrapping with [Jake Paul]. That sounds fun."

Paul, who has been vocal for years along with MVP in encouraging the UFC to increase its fighter pay, acknowledged Strickland's post in a response.

"Sean Strickland I see your texts but are you out of contract?" Paul wrote. "Tell your 'promoter' to call MVP."

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Inside the abrupt ending to A'ja Wilson's historic MVP season
stories.summary: The WNBA Finals will be without five-time MVP A'ja Wilson and the Aces. The script flipped suddenly on the defending champs.
stories.body:
WITH THE HOOD on her black Aces sweatshirt pulled up, A'ja Wilson walked to the dais 40 minutes after the buzzer sounded on the Aces' season. Her black smiley-face slippers clopped against the stairs. She sat down and drummed her fingers on the table as she fielded questions about why the Aces came up short and what the team's future holds.

She looked down at her lap when Chelsea Gray praised her season.

"MVP man, that girl can ball. She can hoop," Gray said, earning a sadness-tinged smile and chuckle from Wilson.

It wasn't the ending Wilson envisioned. She shot just 6-for-19 from the floor on Friday night in Las Vegas, missed three free throws in the fourth quarter, and got her pocket picked with 1:54 to go. The turnover allowed the Valkyries to tie the score with a bucket on the other end.

The defending champions never led again.

On the next possession, Wilson missed a jumper in the lane and the Valkyries scored again to go up by two. A Jackie Young bucket forced overtime, but the Aces were outscored 16-6 and were swept out of the WNBA semifinals with an 87-77 loss.

"I want to do everything I can for my team, and I felt like I did not do that at some points," Wilson said at the dais. "So I think that is going to carry over more so than [missing] the free throw or the missed shots."

Wilson's record-breaking fifth MVP season concluded far sooner than she imagined, on a night when she scored 21 points and grabbed 10 rebounds. All season long, she showcased her evolving game. She's a better shooter, a better facilitator, a better defender. But even her greatness has limits. Injuries to teammates, a suffocating Valkyries defense and a pointing fan in Indiana proved too much for even the greatest to overcome.

A DAY BEFORE the official demise, Wilson wore a double-breasted Aces red Dolce & Gabbana suit and was flanked by her five MVP trophies. She peered through her black-rimmed glasses as she addressed reporters after receiving her record fifth WNBA MVP trophy and unprecedented third in a row.

"It truly means a lot, and so I think that's why I cried a little bit harder on this one," Wilson said Thursday. "Because 15-year-old A'ja wasn't sitting up here dreaming about being a five-time MVP. She wasn't dreaming about being a three-time champion. She was dreaming about surviving this world. For me to sit up here surrounded by these trophies and to be able to play the game of basketball every single day just means a little bit more to me."

Surprised by her teammates and WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert at practice, Wilson doubled over in tears. Her mother, Eva Rakes Wilson, carried in the newest award for her daughter's stuffed trophy case. Engelbert presented a cream-colored old-fashioned phone to Wilson preloaded with congratulatory messages. She heard from her family, former coaches, each of her teammates, her partner Bam Adebayo, and Kamala Harris, the former vice president and Wilson's fellow Alpha Kappa Alpha alum.

"Keep being the example. Keep being you," Dawn Staley told Wilson in her message.

"Little girls around the world, they see you," Lisa Leslie said.

"You are the blueprint of what an elite athlete should strive to be," Sylvia Fowles told her.

"This game needed you. Vegas needed you. We all needed you," Chelsea Gray said.

"Quite frankly, the planet hasn't seen anything like you," Becky Hammon said.

Wilson had come a long way from the young girl in Columbia, South Carolina, who spent her time handing out water bottles to her teammates because she wasn't good enough to get on the floor.

Now she's arguably the best women's basketball player in history.

Wilson dominated the MVP conversation practically from the jump. She dropped 45 points against Connecticut on May 15 and swept the WNBA's Western Conference Player of the Month awards all season.

Other players had their moments of MVP candidacy -- Olivia Miles, Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell -- but their theoretical viability faded as Wilson's inevitability emerged. Again.

"They want to pick someone else, but she won't let them," Adebayo said in an August phone interview. "If you look at the numbers, there's no way you can't. Like how do you give it to someone else?"

Wilson finished the regular season as the league's scoring champion, averaging 26.2 points per game and topping 1,000 points for the second time in her career. She has expanded her playmaking ability and averaged a career-high 3.2 assists per game. Wilson also stepped out on the perimeter and shot a career-best 40.4% from beyond the arc. Her 9.4 win shares led the league, 1.9 higher than second place. Her 32.4 efficiency rating (PER) was similarly dominant with the league's second-highest at 24.1. Wilson has posted four of the WNBA's top seven single-season efficiency ratings from 2023-2026, and is the career PER leader.

When Wilson was awarded her first MVP in 2020, the Aces were swept in the WNBA Finals by Seattle. The young superstar was among the best in the league. It was Hammon's arrival that helped make her the best.

HAMMON WATCHED AS WILSON drilled shots from around the perimeter, far beyond what Hammon thought her natural range was. Hammon had just taken the job as the Aces head coach, and Wilson had flown to San Antonio to meet with her. They'd gone out to dinner at a Brazilian steakhouse the night before so Hammon could get to know her new star. She had a request.

"I asked her to allow me to coach her," Hammon recalled in August. "And coach her hard in front of her teammates, which she agreed to. She's a real one."

The next day, Hammon put Wilson through a workout to get a close look at the talent she wanted to push. She'd seen Wilson's low-post dominance on film, but this version of Wilson was different. She showed Hammon that she was capable of more than she'd put on tape to that point. When Hammon asked why Wilson wasn't more active on the perimeter, Wilson said it wasn't part of the previous system.

"I was like, 'Well, it's about to be part of the system,'" Hammon said.

Wilson consistently showed off that evolution this season. Against the Valkyries on June 21, Golden State guard Tiffany Hayes drove down the lane. Wilson turned her body toward Hayes and bent her knees to prepare to explode upward. As Hayes floated the ball toward the rim, Wilson leapt with her left arm fully outstretched, twisting her body to avoid Hayes as she drove by and swatted the ball.

Jewell Loyd grabbed the deflection and passed the ball back to Wilson, who threw it ahead to Young before sprinting up the court. Young flicked the ball back to a trailing Wilson. The 6-foot-4 center caught the pass in stride, dribbled by her defender, and finished the layup with her left hand.

Just another highlight for the five-time MVP and three-time Defensive Player of the Year.

"She's just extended her game," Hammon said in July. "She's not just a low-block elbow type of player, which she very much was when I first got here. Now, we play her like a big guard a lot of times, and she's just a nightmare matchup for people. I don't know if anybody's found the remedy for her."

Wilson put in the work during her offseason. Unlike many WNBA stars, Wilson doesn't play competitively in the months between WNBA seasons. Fans and competitors alike won't see her in Unrivaled or dominating overseas in the EuroLeague. After the WNBA season ends, she takes a few months off to recharge. And then, when she hears the call of the ball bouncing on the hardwood, Wilson goes to work.

"When it comes to basketball, the way that I view it, like it's just a matter of sharpening tools," Wilson said in July. "You have those tools already in your toolbox. It's just a matter of how you use them and if you can sharpen them."

Wilson has focused during the past three offseasons on navigating the tight windows presented to her on the court. The pirouettes through double-teams, slipping through traffic on drives to the basket, a jab step to create space, a reverse pivot to a face-up jumper, her ability to maneuver within and manipulate cramped spaces elevated her game.

"You'll see her at the elbow now, between the legs, into a combo move," Gray said in August. "You think you got her figured out and the next year she comes with something better."

"I don't want to call her a maniac, but [she's got] the mindset of somebody that is obsessed to be that great and just dominant from all levels," Adebayo said.

THE FIRST REAL SIGN of trouble for Wilson emerged on Aug. 31 when USA Basketball announced she wouldn't play in the FIBA Women's World Cup because of a nagging back injury. She'd missed four games in late June and early July, including the Commissioner's Cup championship against New York, due to an ankle injury, but she'd played at a high level through July and August. Not going to Berlin was the first indication that something was amiss with her body.

The break, however, was good physically and mentally for Wilson. She practiced with her teammates while Young and Gray won a gold medal overseas. As she worked to get healthy, Wilson moved lighter in the gym and the locker room, giving her teammates more glimpses of her humor and goofiness.

"She was just more opened up," Aces forward Cheyenne Parker-Tyus said at shootaround before Game 2 against the Fever. "Throughout the season, she's reserved, you know, because it takes a lot. I think that has to do with just everybody always constantly pulling at her, and the world is literally on her shoulders sometimes. But she was definitely more giddy and more just in a good place. You could tell that she was happy to be home. Sometimes, when you're dealing with injuries and pains, it can affect your mental."

Off the court, Wilson relaxed with her dogs, watched movies with her parents, swam and enjoyed massages. "She got a lot of self-care and relaxation," Rakes Wilson said. "And it shows. She was ready to go."

In the four games following the FIBA break that closed the regular season, Wilson looked rejuvenated, averaging 27.8 points, 8.8 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.3 blocks during the stretch. And in Game 1 against the Fever, Wilson was transcendent: 38 points, 16 rebounds, 4 blocks and 2 steals.

"She's ready to go," Hammon said of Wilson after the Aces' Game 1 102-85 victory. "She understands the stakes always. She was a clinic tonight. There was nothing she didn't do tonight."

Wilson often says, "The crown is heavy." Sometimes it wobbles.

CHAOS ERUPTED SUDDENLY in Game 2 on Sept. 29 in Indiana. Wilson and Fever guard Sophie Cunningham collided in the lane with 4:10 to go in the fourth quarter. Cunningham ended up on the hardwood, and Wilson stumbled forward to regain her balance. Referees called a blocking foul on Cunningham.

An expressionless Wilson walked off the collision. As she approached the basket, she locked eyes with a Fever fan standing and pointing at her. According to another fan in the section, the pointing fan shouted, "That's on you!" referring to the foul just called on Cunningham.

Wilson accelerated toward the fan, crossed the white painted boundary of the baseline and bent toward him. She yelled, "You don't point at me!" Her teammates and coaches rushed to pull her away. Wilson was assessed a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct.

After the game, Wilson said she apologized to her teammates for the technical but defended her actions. "I try to play my game ... but if I am just walking, just got the foul, I'm chilling and I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said," she said. "I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone. That is unacceptable. You don't step toward me. You never should sit and point at me. That there is unacceptable."

For the entirety of Wilson's athletic career, she's been known for her charisma, humility and gratitude. The outburst in Gainbridge was discombobulating largely because Wilson isn't known for fiery displays. She celebrates -- who doesn't love a good A'ja stomp after an and-1? -- makes faces and complains to refs as much as the next player. What happened in Indianapolis was something different.

It was an out-of-character moment toward the end of an out-of-character performance for Wilson. In the Aces' 99-89 Game 2 loss, she had 22 points and nine rebounds, but it was far from the dominance she displayed in Game 1. And the moment between her and the fan she confronted became the first significant controversy of her career.

She was criticized by some on social media for overreacting. Cunningham, who declined an interview request through her agent for this story, told Wilson to "grow up" on her podcast.

"I could care less about what anyone has to say about me or anything they want to write about me or comment," Wilson said. "No one's ever lived this life that I'm living, so they can never have any input that would make my mind go into another space. I really don't care about it."

Others -- teammates and family -- empathized with her reaction during an intense game in a hostile road arena.

"That's not A'ja," Rakes Wilson said. "She's managed in the whole nine years of her career not to do what she did, so it had to be something. And I'll be honest with you, I don't care what he said. That's not important to me. What's important to me was she felt unsafe, she felt threatened, and she felt disrespected."

Wilson received no additional punishment for her actions, and neither did the Aces players who left the bench to pull her back. The Aces won Game 3 at home and the world kept spinning. But the Aces and Wilson didn't win again.

IN GAME 1 against the Valkyries, the Aces managed just 60 points, their lowest total of the season. Jewell Loyd hurt her leg in the third quarter and didn't return. Game 2 was closer even without Loyd, but a furious rally came up short. And suddenly the reigning champions were facing elimination in Game 3.

Wilson arrived at her home arena on Friday in a white T-shirt and shorts. She sidestepped the pomp and circumstance that's come to characterize WNBA arrivals. No glitzy outfit. No pregame autographs. No trophies. Her parents lifted Wilson's MVP trophy for the crowd in a pregame ceremony, while Wilson warmed up with her teammates.

"The individual award is going to be what it's going to be," Wilson said. "I love it. I cherish it. I don't take it for granted. But the main goal is always going to be a championship."

For a half, the Aces looked like they could keep their goal intact. But they were outscored 17-7 in the third quarter and then lost a late lead in the fourth. Shots clanged off the rim. Turnovers mounted. The Aces were done.

With her parents and Adebayo waiting, Wilson sat at the podium and insisted they were only done for now.

"It's just not our time, and I'm OK with that," she said. "I'm at peace with the great things we did do. I can't harp on this game too much. I'm just very happy that our team was locked in and we showed up for one another. Obviously the outcome's not what we wanted, but we're still champions at heart. We're gonna have another opportunity. I guarantee you that."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen calls on F1 to ditch sprint races 'where you can't pass' after Singapore GP win
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has called on Formula 1 to stop hosting sprint races on circuits where overtaking is difficult after very little passing took place during Saturday's 20-lap sprint in Singapore.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has called on Formula 1 to stop hosting sprint races on circuits where overtaking is difficult after very little passing took place during Saturday's 20-lap sprint in Singapore.

This weekend is the first time F1 has run its sprint format in Singapore -- a circuit where overtaking is notoriously difficult -- since the Saturday races were introduced to the sport in 2021.

Singapore is the last of six sprint weekends this season, with F1 increasing the number to 10 in 2027, including one at the Monaco Grand Prix where overtaking is even more difficult than in Singapore.

Four-time champion Verstappen, who won Saturday's sprint race after taking the lead when George Russell crashed in front of him on the opening lap, said the format should be reserved purely for circuits where passing is possible.

"I think we shouldn't host a sprint where you can't pass," Verstappen said. "If you have tracks where you can race and can overtake [it works], but of course in some places you cannot pass and we are going to have sprints there also next year.

"I'm fine. I just do my thing and then that's it, right? But yeah, it's not what I like."

Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc agreed, adding that street circuits, such as Singapore and his home race in Monaco, should not be considered as sprint venues.

"I don't think it makes sense to have any sprint races on city tracks in general," he said. "And we probably should use these sprints to have them on tracks where it's easy to overtake, where you can have a lot of racing action and actually add something to the weekend.

"Whereas here or Monaco, I don't think it adds anything to the weekend."

Lewis Hamilton, who finished second in Saturday's sprint, said the only reason the 20-lap race provided any entertainment was because it rained ahead of the start.

"I thought it was fun, but if it was dry, that would have been probably the most boring race for you to have watched," the seven-time champion said.

"It was the wet, the rain that made it exciting. So if you can always make it rain, then it's always going to be a great sprint race. But otherwise, it'd probably just been straightforward tyre management, everyone sticking behind each other."

- Max Verstappen claims sprint victory at Singapore Grand Prix, George Russell crashes out of lead

- Singapore Grand Prix: George Russell crashes out of sprint after taking early lead

- 'Watch Teletubbies, not F1': Toto Wolff hits back at 'brainless' Kimi Antonelli driver favouritism claims

Hamilton also called for the Singapore circuit layout to be changed to encourage more overtaking in the future.

"I love the race here -- I really do love the race -- but I was just saying to Max, I think they need to change the track to maybe a longer straight somewhere in order to allow it to be truly a great racing circuit, because I think it has the potential to be a great racing circuit.

"It's a great track to drive over a single lap and qualifying, but there literally just isn't many [places to pass]. There's like one place, I guess, really that you could potentially get close to overtake. But then in other places like [Turn] 16, the crest in the middle of the track, sparks come up because the track isn't particularly flat.

"I don't know if it's for the rain or whatever it is, but I think there's some adjustments that can be made to make this 100% like a great circuit. But whether or not they're going to do that, I don't know."

Verstappen said the lack of overtaking in Singapore is not helped by the ineffectiveness of the power unit's overtake mode, which allows a chasing driver to access full electric power for more of the lap than the car in front.

"Also the problem we have at the moment is with the overtake mode, it barely does anything here," Verstappen added.

"You don't really gain a lot on the straights. So also that with how all the rules are at the moment, with our lovely batteries, it just doesn't do much. You can't even get super close or have a massive overspeed at the moment.

"So I of course fully agree we need to have a longer straight or more of a proper hairpin to overtake. But even with that also, we need a bigger delta on the straight."
